{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Read the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Parse revenue as float: remove commas and cast to float
# But no commas found, so just cast to float
# Also, convert any '999999.99' to NaN to exclude QA orders
df['revenue_float'] = pd.to_numeric(df['revenue'], errors='coerce')

# Mark QA orders (revenue = 999999.99) as NaN
qa_mask = (df['revenue_float'] == 999999.99)
df.loc[qa_mask, 'revenue_float'] = None

# Drop QA rows
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=['revenue_float'])

# Now, filter to completed and converted = 1
# But note: there are 21 rows where converted=1 but status != completed
# These are invalid — if converted=1, status must be completed
# So remove them
valid_converted = (df_clean['converted'] == 1) & (df_clean['status'] == 'completed')
df_final = df_clean[valid_converted].copy()

# Now, compute average revenue per converted order by channel, stratified by segment
# First, pivot to get channel as columns
pivot = df_final.pivot_table(index='customer_segment', columns='channel', values='revenue_float', aggfunc='mean').round(2)

# Compute difference: email - paid_search
pivot['diff'] = pivot['email'] - pivot['paid_search']

# Print the difference for the returning segment explicitly — this is the key value
# We must print the exact number used in evidence
returned_diff = pivot.loc['returning', 'diff']
print(f'Exact difference in returning segment (email - paid_search): {returned_diff}')

# Also print the raw averages for evidence
email_returning = pivot.loc['returning', 'email']
paid_search_returning = pivot.loc['returning', 'paid_search']
print(f'Email average revenue (returning): {email_returning}')
print(f'Paid_search average revenue (returning): {paid_search_returning}')

# Print the full difference table for context
print('\nFull difference table:')
print(pivot[['diff']])

# Final confirmation: print the value to be used in evidence
print(f'Final value for evidence: {returned_diff}')"}
